extraction.name: LUMA
extraction.description: A benchmark multimodal dataset for learning from uncertain data, containing image, audio, and text modalities with tools to inject controlled uncertainty and baseline uncertainty quantification models.

extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled from three modalities collected from different sources: images from CIFAR-10/100, audio segments extracted and validated from The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, Mozilla Common Voice, plus some voluntary recordings, and text passages generated with Gemma-7B Instruct based on class labels. The modalities were then aligned by class and compiled into a clean dataset with tools for controlled uncertainty injection.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include CIFAR-10/100 images; audio/text parallel corpora The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice; 73 additional voluntary audio recordings; and text generated by Google's Gemma-7B Instruct model.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset toolkit supports manipulation of uncertainty through adjustable parameters including data diversity control, sample-level noise injection, structured label corruption using nearest-class reassignment, and out-of-distribution sample injection.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio samples were extracted from aligned transcripts, plural forms were considered, anonymized and trimmed for contributed recordings, automatically transcribed with Whisper Large V3 for validation, and false negatives were manually reviewed. Text samples were generated and validated by masking label occurrences and reclassifying with Gemma-7B Instruct. Images were aligned with other modalities and supplemented with EDM-generated images to support diversity control.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual annotation was used for audio validation on samples flagged after automatic validation. Annotators answered whether an audio sample said the target word, allowing extra 's' or 'es'. Samples confirmed by both annotators were accepted and conflicting cases were rejected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Audio validation combined automatic and manual validation. Positive automatic predictions were accepted without manual review due to low expected false positives; negative predictions were manually checked for selected classes. Annotation agreement was 71.61%, and only samples with agreement from both annotators were accepted while conflicts were rejected.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators who were colleagues: M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors with advanced to fluent English knowledge.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI Whisper Large V3; Gemma-7B Instruct
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is open-source, includes a Python package and data compilation pipeline, and is intended to be extended with additional modalities and community contributions in the future.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender-related class labels and associated bias-sensitive content, specifically man, woman, boy, and girl.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support development of trustworthy and robust multimodal machine learning, especially for safety-critical applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The text modality may contain offensive biases, stereotypes, and factual inaccuracies due to LLM generation. The authors identified substantial gender bias in texts for the classes man, woman, boy, and girl, and attempted to mitigate it by reconstructing prompts and filtering biased outputs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Audio data may include misaligned segments, noisy samples, or strong accents; text data generated by an LLM may contain factual inaccuracies and biases; the dataset is intended as a benchmark for uncertainty quantification and should not be used as a source of knowledge or information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, development, evaluation, and experimentation for multimodal learning and uncertainty quantification, including training and testing with 500 training and 100 testing samples per class, plus OOD detection studies.

name.evidence: We propose LUMA, a unique multimodal dataset, featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data.

Based on the collected samples from the 3 modalities (image, text, audio), we first compiled a clean version of the dataset with minimal uncertainty.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We prioritized flexibility, offering multiple options for controlling uncertainty through adjustable parameters such as data diversity, sample-level noise, label corruption, and the injection of out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: 73 additional recordings of pronunciations belonging to 4 classes ... were anonymized, trimmed, and added to the dataset. ... The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI’s Whisper Large V3 model [29] for audio transcription, and transcribed the extracted audio samples. If the transcription corresponded to the class label (or its plural form), then we considered the sample as valid. Otherwise, the sample was sent for manual validation. ... To validate that the generated texts accurately represent the labels, we masked all label occurrences in the text and fed the masked text back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model, asking it to classify the text into one of the labels.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: For manual validation, we decided to check only the classes, which did not have more than 800 samples... The interface provided the audio sample, with the prompt "Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra ’s’ or ’es’ in the pronunciation is okay.)" and answer options of "Yes" or "No". ... In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators. We got 71.61% annotation agreement and accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Since most of the audio data is collected from forced alignments, it is possible to have misaligned audio segments, which could introduce additional noise to the dataset. Moreover, since part of the audio samples are from voluntary contributions, there can be very noisy samples, which are hard to interpret, or audio samples with a strong accent, which again can be hard to interpret. ... Since textual data was generated using an LLM, we recognize that the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies, or biases... LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information.
